subject: chemistry
title: Properties of simple molecular substances
key_idea: Simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points because only the weak forces between molecules are overcome, not the strong covalent bonds inside them. Bigger molecules have stronger forces, so higher boiling points. They do not conduct electricity.

blocks.text: Small molecules are usually gases or liquids at room temperature. This section covers why, and what is and is not broken when they melt or boil.

items.meaning: A substance made of small molecules, such as water, methane and chlorine.
Weak forces of attraction between molecules.

items.text: The substance is made of small, separate molecules.
There are only weak intermolecular forces between the molecules.
Little energy is needed to overcome these forces, so the melting and boiling points are low.

items: The covalent bonds inside each molecule are strong.
When the substance melts or boils, the intermolecular forces are overcome. The covalent bonds are **not** broken.
Intermolecular forces are weak compared with covalent bonds.

diagram.alt: Sort each change into whether intermolecular forces are overcome or covalent bonds are broken.

items.text: Nitrogen and hydrogen react to make ammonia

diagram.prompt: What is happening to the molecules? Sort each change.

items: Simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points.
Melting and boiling overcome intermolecular forces, not covalent bonds.
Never write about breaking covalent bonds to explain a low boiling point.

blocks.text: Intermolecular forces get stronger as molecules get larger. This section covers the trends in the halogens and the alkanes.

items: Going down Group 7 the molecules increase in size.
So the intermolecular forces increase.
So more energy is needed to overcome them, and the boiling point increases.
The same trend holds for alkanes: the more carbon atoms in the molecule, the higher the boiling point.

blocks.text: Poly(ethene) has much larger molecules than methane. It has stronger intermolecular forces, so it is a solid and methane is a gas.

items: Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces.
Stronger forces need more energy to overcome, so the boiling point is higher.

blocks.text: Simple molecular substances do not conduct electricity. This section covers why.

items: To conduct, a substance needs charged particles that are free to move.
Molecules have no overall electric charge.
They have no ions and no delocalised electrons that can move.
So they do not conduct electricity, as solids, liquids or gases.

blocks.text: A melting point or boiling point belongs to many molecules together. One molecule on its own does not have one.

items: Molecules have no overall charge, so simple molecular substances do not conduct.
Melting point and boiling point are bulk properties of many molecules.

checks.q: Explain why ammonia has a low boiling point.
checks.a: It is a simple molecular substance with weak intermolecular forces between its molecules. Little energy is needed to overcome these forces.

checks.q: Explain the increase in boiling points going down Group 7.
checks.a: The molecules increase in size, so the intermolecular forces increase, so more energy is needed to overcome them.

checks.q: Explain why simple molecular substances do not conduct electricity.
checks.a: The molecules have no overall electric charge, and there are no ions or free electrons to carry charge.

worked_example.question: This question is about ammonia, NH₃. Explain why ammonia has a low boiling point. You should refer to structure and bonding in your answer.
answer_points: Ammonia has small molecules, a simple molecular structure.
So little energy is needed to overcome the intermolecular forces.
worked_example.tip: Do not refer to breaking covalent bonds. That is not accepted for the second or third marks.

worked_example.question: Chlorine exists as diatomic molecules. In a molecule, two chlorine atoms are joined by a covalent bond. Explain why chlorine is a gas, rather than a liquid, at room temperature.
answer_points: There are intermolecular forces, forces between the molecules.
These forces are weak, or take little energy to break.
The boiling point is below room temperature, it has a low boiling point.
worked_example.tip: Any two score a mark each. If the answer is about breaking any type of bond, the first two points cannot score.

worked_example.question: Some information about phosphorus compounds is shown. Phosphorus trichloride, PCl₃: melting point -94 °C, boiling point 76 °C. Phosphorus pentachloride, PCl₅: melting point 161 °C, boiling point 167 °C. Phosphorus trifluoride, PF₃: melting point -152 °C, boiling point -102 °C. Put a ring around the compound with the weakest intermolecular forces: phosphorus trichloride, phosphorus pentachloride or phosphorus trifluoride. Explain your answer using information from the table.
answer_points: The weakest intermolecular forces need the least energy to break, or the least energy to separate the molecules.
Less energy to break the forces means a lower melting point and boiling point.
Phosphorus trifluoride has the lowest melting point and boiling point in the table, and is a gas at room temperature.
worked_example.tip: Choose the compound, then give any two reasons linking the forces to the energy and the melting or boiling point.

worked_example.question: Tin(IV) chloride, SnCl₄, is covalently bonded. Tin(II) oxide, SnO, is ionically bonded. SnCl₄ has a melting point of –33 °C and SnO has a melting point of 1080 °C. Explain, in terms of structure and bonding, why SnCl₄ has a much lower melting point than SnO.
answer_points: There is attraction between molecules (intermolecular forces) in tin(IV) chloride.
Tin(II) oxide has a giant ionic structure.
The attraction between particles in tin(IV) chloride is weaker.
worked_example.tip: The covalent bonds inside the SnCl₄ molecules are not broken when it melts.

worked_example.question: Hydrogen chloride and magnesium chloride have different types of bonding and have different structures. Explain why magnesium chloride has a much higher melting point than hydrogen chloride. Refer to structure and bonding in your answer.
answer_points: Hydrogen chloride is simple molecular (simple covalent).
Magnesium chloride is a giant ionic lattice.
There is strong electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions in magnesium chloride.
There are only weak intermolecular forces between hydrogen chloride molecules.
Much more energy is needed to break the ionic bonds in magnesium chloride than to overcome the forces between hydrogen chloride molecules.
worked_example.tip: Five of these points score. Never refer to breaking the covalent bonds in hydrogen chloride.

items: Relative molecular mass, Mᵣ, is the sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms in a molecule.
In general, the melting and boiling points of simple molecular substances increase as Mᵣ increases.
In the halogens, Mᵣ rises from 38 for F₂ to 254 for I₂, and the boiling point rises with it.
